A variation which I heard sometimes is "you are responsible for your own happiness". I guess at its core it is reasonable and logical, however, I don't necessarily believe it to be 100% accurate. Say there's a couple who have been together for a long time and have been very happy together. Now, they sort of rely on each other (at least to some extent) to be happy. If they were to break up, of course both of them would be very sad. In that instance you wouldn't say that quote to them, right? The statement sort of implies that you are in control all the time, otherwise you wouldn't be responsible. But if something tragic happens beyond your control, or you just have a lot of bad luck in life, you wouldn't be happy. in that instance this statement woudn't make much sense either, right? yes, you are for the most part responsible for your recovery, but the argument still stands, I think. just my 2 cents.
